abstract.text:
This paper proposes a real-time approach for longterm inertial navigation based only on an Inertial Measurement
Unit (IMU) for self-localizing wheeled robots. The approach
builds upon two components: 1) a robust detector that uses
recurrent deep neural networks to dynamically detect a variety
of situations of interest, such as zero velocity or no lateral
slip; and 2) a state-of-the-art Kalman filter which incorporates
this knowledge as pseudo-measurements for localization. Evaluations on a publicly available car dataset demonstrates that
the proposed scheme may achieve a final precision of 20 m for
a 21 km long trajectory of a vehicle driving for over an hour,
equipped with an IMU of moderate precision (the gyro drift
rate is 10 deg/h). To our knowledge, this is the first paper which
combines sophisticated deep learning techniques with state-ofthe-art filtering methods for pure inertial navigation on wheeled
vehicles and as such opens up for novel data-driven inertial
navigation techniques. Moreover, albeit taylored for IMU-only
based localization, our method may be used as a component
for self-localization of wheeled robots equipped with a more
complete sensor suite.

sections.summary: Introduces the paper's goal: long-term IMU-only inertial navigation for wheeled robots. The contributions combine recurrent deep neural network detectors for motion profiles with an invariant extended Kalman filter that treats detected profiles as pseudo-measurements. Related work contrasts high-precision INS, MEMS drift, sensor fusion, ZUPT, and recent deep-learning pedestrian inertial navigation, positioning RINS-W as the first to combine deep learning with state-of-the-art filtering for pure inertial wheeled-vehicle navigation.

sections.summary: Defines the inertial navigation state and IMU measurement model, then introduces four wheeled-vehicle motion profiles encoded as a binary vector: zero velocity, zero angular velocity, zero lateral velocity, and zero vertical velocity. It explains why zero velocity does not imply zero angular velocity for cars with shock absorbers, and separates the profiles into zero-velocity constraints that can correct biases and attitude versus motion constraints that improve long-term accuracy.

sections.summary: Describes the RINS-W system as two blocks: an LSTM-based detector that outputs binary motion-profile scores from raw IMU signals, and a right invariant extended Kalman filter that fuses IMU dynamics with detected profiles as pseudo-measurements. The detector uses four LSTMs with thresholded outputs. The IEKF state includes pose, velocity, and IMU biases; propagation is modified when zero-velocity or zero-angular-velocity profiles are detected, and updates use the corresponding pseudo-measurements. Initialization requires a short stop to estimate biases and attitude.
sections.title: RINS-W Detector and Invariant Extended Kalman Filter

sections.summary: Evaluates RINS-W on the complex urban LiDAR dataset using an Xsens MTi-300 IMU at 100 Hz. Training uses urban06–urban14 and testing uses urban15–urban17. The section details LSTM implementation, thresholds, noise covariances, training, error metrics, trajectory results, discussion, and detector evaluation. RINS-W achieves a 20 m final error on the 73-minute urban16 sequence, outperforms wheel odometry, and competes with or outperforms odometry aided by a much more accurate fiber-optic gyro. Ablations show lateral and vertical velocity updates are important for avoiding divergence, and the learned detector outperforms an ideal AMVD for zero-velocity detection. The conclusion emphasizes IMU-only operation, parallel safety use, and future work on covariance learning and generalization.
sections.title: Car Dataset Evaluation, Discussion, and Conclusion

sections.summary: Provides the mathematical background and filter Jacobians used by RINS-W. Appendix A defines the Lie group SE2(3), maps uncertainty into the Lie algebra se2(3), and gives the closed-form exponential map. Appendix B gives the propagation Jacobians for the IEKF and the measurement Jacobians for zero-velocity, zero-angular-velocity, zero-lateral-velocity, and zero-vertical-velocity updates, including how rows are zeroed when those profiles are detected.
